# MCQs generated by the generate-then-validate SLM pipeline are generally answerable and unambiguous, as judged by seven human experts

> **Claim** · [All claims](index.md)
> **Evidence** · 1 study · design `r2` · `q3`

## Subclaims
`q3 i?` Seven middle-school science teachers showed substantial agreement on the correct answers to 64 generated MCQs, and only 1.6% of the MCQs were deemed unanswerable by majority vote. [→ human-answers-1](#human-answers-1)

## Evidence

### human-answers-1

Yumou Wei, John Stamper, and Paulo F. Carvalho. 2026. Generate-Then-Validate: A Novel Question Generation Approach Using Small Language Models. In LAK26: 16th International Learning Analytics and Knowledge Conference (LAK 2026), Bergen, Norway. ACM, New York, NY, USA. https://doi.org/10.1145/3785022.3785100

`q3 · i?` · `design · r2`

Human evaluation study: seven middle-school science teachers answered 64 MCQs generated from eight AP Environmental Science learning objectives, each with a 'none of the above' option added. Their Fleiss' kappa of 0.70 indicates "the generated MCQs are generally answerable and unambiguous".

> "The seven human judges achieved a substantial agreement [21] with each other (Fleiss' kappa = 0.70), indicating that the generated MCQs are generally answerable and unambiguous."
